Direct answer｜The work of gambling dealers can be broadly divided into three categories. First, game operation and dealing: standing or sitting behind the table, opening and controlling the table according to the specific game rules and procedures, dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to each player and operating other gambling equipment, starting and controlling games and equipment and announcing winning numbers or colors, dealing cards to the house hand and comparing with players' hands to determine the winner, applying rule variants in card games such as poker, dealing as part of a team in games such as baccarat or craps, and joining a game when needed to make up the minimum number of players. Second, chips and wagering and settlement: greeting customers and making them feel welcome, confirming before play begins that all players have placed their bets, receiving and verifying and recording customers' cash wagers, exchanging bills for chips or coins, paying winnings or collecting losing stakes according to the rules, calculating player wins and losses or scanning winning tickets to determine amounts, referring customers to the cage cashier to collect winnings, and opening and closing the cash float and table. Third, table supervision and records and collaboration: checking the cards and equipment used in the game to ensure they are in good condition, supervising staff and monitoring tables to keep the game secure, seating customers at the table, guiding new dealers, preparing and submitting collection reports, and answering questions about game rules and casino policies. The three categories of work link in cycles: open the table and check the cards — greet and confirm bets — deal and determine the winner — collect and pay and exchange — open and close the float and record — monitor the table and report anomalies.

O*NET occupational profile highlights｜The official scope of O*NET-SOC 39-3011.00 “Gambling Dealers” is: Operate table games. Stand or sit behind table and operate games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment. Distribute winnings or collect players' money or chips. May compare the house's hand against players' hands. Of the 21 tasks given in the occupational profile, 16 are core tasks: pay winnings or collect losing stakes according to the specific game rules and procedures; greet customers and make them feel welcome; exchange bills for chips or coins; confirm before play begins that all players have placed their bets; check the cards and equipment used in the game to ensure they are in good condition; deal cards to the house hand and compare with players' hands to determine the winner (such as in blackjack); stand behind the table and dispense the appropriate number of cards to each player; apply rule variants in card games such as poker; receive and verify and record customers' cash wagers; run dice and roulette and card or keno and other gambling games according to all applicable rules and regulations; work as part of a dealer team in games such as baccarat or craps; start and control games and gambling equipment and announce winning numbers or colors; calculate player wins and losses or scan winning tickets presented by customers to determine the winning amount; open and close the cash reserve and table; answer questions about game rules and casino policies; refer customers to the cage cashier to collect winnings. There are another 5 supplemental tasks: supervise staff and monitor tables to keep the game secure; seat customers at the table; train new dealers; prepare collection reports for the supervisor; participate in games at the gambling establishment to provide the minimum number of players at the table.

entries.answer: According to O*NET-SOC 39-3011.00, this occupation operates table games: standing or sitting behind the table and operating games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment; distributing winnings or collecting players' money or chips; and may compare the house's hand against players' hands. The work includes paying out or collecting according to game rules and procedures, greeting customers, exchanging bills for chips or coins, confirming bets before play begins, checking the cards and equipment used, dealing cards to the house hand and comparing to determine the winner, dealing cards to players, applying rule variants in games such as poker, receiving and verifying and recording cash wagers, running games such as dice and roulette and cards or keno according to the rules, dealing as part of a team in team games, starting and controlling games and equipment and announcing winning numbers or colors, calculating wins and losses or scanning winning tickets, opening and closing the cash float and table, answering questions about game rules and casino policies, referring customers to the cage cashier, supervising staff and monitoring tables, seating customers, training new dealers, preparing collection reports, and joining a game when needed to make up the minimum number of players. What this page describes is a legal position in jurisdictions such as the United States that allow licensed gambling; in mainland China, apart from the state-approved lotteries issued in accordance with the law, gambling and operating casinos are strictly prohibited by the Criminal Law and other laws.

subject.summary: Gambling Dealers (O*NET-SOC 39-3011.00, Gambling Dealers) operate games of chance at tables in licensed gambling establishments: standing or sitting behind the table and operating games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment; distributing winnings or collecting players' money or chips; and may compare the house's hand against players' hands. The work includes paying out or collecting according to game rules and procedures, greeting customers, exchanging bills for chips or coins, confirming bets before play begins, checking the cards and equipment used, dealing cards to the house hand and comparing to determine the winner, dealing cards to players, applying rule variants in games such as poker, receiving and verifying and recording cash wagers, running games such as dice and roulette and cards or keno according to the rules, dealing as part of a team in team games, starting and controlling games and equipment and announcing winning numbers or colors, calculating wins and losses or scanning winning tickets, opening and closing the cash float and table, answering questions about game rules and casino policies, referring customers to the cage cashier, supervising staff and monitoring tables, seating customers, training new dealers, preparing collection reports, and joining a game when needed to make up the minimum number of players. Official definition text: Operate table games. Stand or sit behind table and operate games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment. Distribute winnings or collect players' money or chips. May compare the house's hand against players' hands.
